title: 1871 Chicago is a city of wood again
items: Outside downtown, nine buildings in ten are now wood frame, as an 1868 count of the city's buildings found; brick and stone stay in the business centre and the better South Side streets.
Frame houses wear painted weatherboard, mostly white with some buff, grey and unpainted, so they no longer read as stone.
Neighbourhood corner shops are two-storey frame stores; every building stays where it stood.
